newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH 1996 ELECTRICITY CONSUMPTION UP 1.6 PCT.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH 1996 ELECTRICITY CONSUMPTION UP 1.6 PCT.

text.p: Finnish electricity consumption
grew 1.6 percent to 70 billion kilowatt hours (kWh) in 1996 on
1995, the Finnish Electricity Association said on Friday.
"Adjusted for calendar days and temperature fluctuations,
1996 electricity consumption rose 0.3 percent, which was
clearly less than ... the previous year's adjusted rise of 2.1
percent," it said in a statement.
Electricity consumption is expected to increase by about
two to three percent a year throughout the 1990s, the
association said.
Industry accounted for 53 percent of total electricity
consumption in 1996, households and agriculture for a good 25
percent, and services and the public sector for over 17
percent, it said.
Combined generation of heat and electricity accounted for
over 32 percent of total consumption, nuclear power for almost
27 percent, condensation power for over 19 percent, hydropower
for almost 17 percent and net imports for five percent, it
said.
Owing to dry conditions in Sweden and Norway, Finland
exported more electric power to its western neighbours than it
has in many years, the association said.
Electricity exports to Sweden and Norway were 17 times
higher in 1996 than in 1995, while electric power imports from
those countries fell to a fifth of the 1995 level, it said.
Only in 1969, 1979, 1980 and 1982 has Finland exported more
electricity to Norway and Sweden than it has imported, it said.
Electricity imports from Russia were stable. Finland has
imported more than four billion kilowatt hours of electricity
from Russia every year since 1983, the association said.
